The old text claimed the candidate 'claims no authority', which the repository's own positive control had contradicted since before this change - CONF-I1-POS has always carried required_authority_type on the proposal. Two things need your judgement, and neither is whether the rewrite is correct. First: Phase I closed on 2026-08-27 and contracts/phases.json pins PRD.md so a closed phase cannot narrow its own definition. I moved that pin. Should a closed phase carry a requirement edited after its terminal, or should the successor campaign carry it? Second: the two new clauses are not registered as SPEC.md predicates, so PRD.md now requires something SPEC.md does not state. Registering them honestly moves the F2 gate from 44 predicates to 46 and from 8 open to 10, which makes the exit visibly further away.

SVC-ASSET-4 retitled and corrected. It still carried the retired 'A proposal claims no authority' clause and cited a PRD.md defeating case that no longer reads that way. Two of the three current defeating cases are unserved by the participant, and the clause now says so.

why_it_matters: The requirement was satisfiable by depositing a record nobody ever read. That is the failure mode the whole system is built against - a model produces something, the record says it happened, and no human is in the loop at any point. Requiring an operator surface puts the human back in the path by contract rather than by hope. The authority half matters for a different reason: the old text described a wish rather than a rule. Saying the candidate 'claims no authority' asks the model to be well-behaved. Saying the session asserts authority and the record refuses to honor it, because an instance has no identity a grant can attach to, is something a check can enforce - and the check now refuses the escape hatch of a session declaring itself CONTINUOUS to keep a grant.
what_could_defeat_it: A reading where the rewritten PROD-I-1 makes any Phase I exit clause easier. I could not find one and the witness could not either, but neither of us is the owner of that judgement.
The position that a closed phase's definition should never move at all, in which case the correct shape is a Phase II requirement and contracts/phases.json should be reverted to the 2026-08-27 pin.
